claim.pdf_says: "D.6.2   Recursive and initial programs" is printed at the same typographic rank as "D.6.1   Compilation group and run unit organization" (page 1071) — both are third-level clauses under D.6.
claim.markdown_says: ## D.6.2 Recursive and initial programs   (while page 1071 has '### D.6.1 Compilation group and run unit organization')
claim.why_it_matters: D.6.2 is promoted to the same markdown level as its parent D.6, so it reads as a sibling of D.6 rather than a subclause of it. Outline-driven navigation and any tooling that reconstructs clause numbering from heading depth gets the wrong parent.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. The claim's two literal quotes are accurate (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43210 is '## D.6.2 Recursive and initial programs'; :42983 is '### D.6.1 Compilation group and run unit organization'), but every load-bearing inference from them fails. (1) NO TEXT IS LOST. Rendered p1076 at 300dpi: the printed heading is the bold line 'D.6.2 Recursive and initial programs'. The markdown carries that string verbatim on line 32 of the page unit, preceded by its anchor ''. Nothing is missing, reflowed, or altered; the kind 'missing-heading' is a misnomer for a difference in '#' count alone. (2) THE PDF PREMISE IS FALSE. I rendered p1071 to check the typography the claim rests on. ISO 1989:2023 prints annex clause headings in ONE flat style: on p1071, 'D.6 Compilation group and run unit organization and communication', 'D.6.1 Compilation group and run unit organization' and 'D.6.1.1 Source level organization' are all set in the SAME bold face at the SAME size, with the same indent — there is no typographic rank distinction between a clause and its own subclause. So D.6.2 being 'at the same typographic rank as D.6.1' is trivially true and carries no information: it is also at the same rank as D.6 and as D.6.1.1. Printed depth is conveyed SOLELY by the dotted clause number, which the transcription preserves exactly (in the heading text and in the anchor slug). The PDF therefore encodes no heading-depth signal for the markdown to have lost. (3) THE HARM IS NOT REACHABLE. Markdown '#' depth in this transcription does not encode the outline anywhere, so there is no working scheme for D.6.2 to break. Measured over all 2435 numbered headings in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: the offset (heading depth minus dotted-number depth) is spread across -3 (144), -2 (392), -1 (1058), 0 (769), +1 (72) — 97% deviate from the most common convention, and 930 headings use '##' for a clause that would need a deeper level. On top of that the file interleaves 1261 '## Page NNNN' markers and 941 level-1 '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' banners, so any outline reconstruction is already defeated by page furniture before reaching D.6.2. Clause numbering is recovered from the heading TEXT ('D.6.2') and the anchor ('section-d-6-2'), never from depth. (4) THE CLAIM INVERTS WHICH HEADING IS ANOMALOUS. Within this very clause the transcription uses '##' for D.6, D.6.1.2, D.6.1.3, D.6.2, D.6.3, D.6.3.3, D.6.3.4, D.6.3.5, D.6.3.6, D.6.4, D.6.4.4 and D.6.5. D.6.2 at '##' is the LOCAL NORM; it is D.6.1 at '###' that departs from its neighbours. The claim also miscasts the hierarchy: D.6.1 and D.6.2 are the direct children of D.6, not 'third-level clauses under D.6'. This is markdown formatting with no counterpart in the source document, at a 97% document-wide baseline rate, with zero change in meaning or content. It is not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: No discrepancy. The heading 'D.6.2 Recursive and initial programs' is present in the markdown verbatim as printed on p1076, with its anchor. The only difference is the markdown '#' count, which is not a property of the PDF at all: ISO prints D.6, D.6.1, D.6.1.1 and D.6.2 in one identical bold style, conveying depth only through the dotted clause number, which the transcription preserves. Heading depth in specs/ISO_COBOL.md is non-hierarchical throughout (97% of 2435 numbered headings deviate from the dominant convention; 1261 '## Page NNNN' and 941 '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' furniture headings are interleaved), so no outline semantics exist to be broken here. If normalized heading depth is ever wanted, it is a whole-document mechanical pass driven by the dotted numbers, not a p1076 finding.
